dashboard-report.name: Dashboard report
dashboard-report.description: Block type that lets a workflow fill the dashboard result from config fields, plus the editor's AI proposal for those fields.

goals.name: Goals
goals.description: Goals with projects, work packages and milestones, TODO planning (size, effort, question/decision), workflows on a goal and the goal guard. Off: goal pages and planning disappear, the data is kept.

run-tokens.name: Run tokens
run-tokens.description: A workflow that asks for it (metadata.permissions: ["read"]) gets a read-only token for the duration of its run (MYSURICATES_RUN_TOKEN) and may read the allowlisted overview: workflows, runs, TODOs, projects, skills, goals, audits, learning. Only switchable in the startup configuration.

chains.name: Chains
chains.description: Chains several workflows into a pipeline that runs one after another.

assistant.name: Assistant
assistant.description: Chat assistant and page suggestions that can read and edit platform objects.

learning.name: Insights & learning
learning.description: Run insights, recommendations and statistics per block type.

memory.name: Workflow memory
memory.description: Knowledge collected from finished runs and injected into later runs.

audit.name: Audit center
audit.description: Findings from audit workflows, with reports and promotion to TODOs.

bpmn.name: BPMN export/import
bpmn.description: Exports workflows as BPMN and reads MySuricates BPMN exports back in.

integrations.name: Integrations
integrations.description: External services (GitHub, Jira, Trello, Google, Confluence, Taskwarrior) via OAuth, plus integration blocks, TODO tracker export and calendar.

http-api.name: HTTP API connection
http-api.description: Outbound HTTP calls from integration blocks to services you enter yourself (base URL + optional auth header, several services as named connections).

webhooks.name: Webhooks
webhooks.description: Inbound webhook triggers that start workflows from outside.

remote-access.name: Remote access
remote-access.description: Remote access to this instance via Tailscale.

terminal.name: Run terminal
terminal.description: Interactive terminal into a run's container over WebSocket.

staging.name: Stable & test instances
staging.description: Stable and test instances in Docker, including definition sync between instances.

mcp.name: MCP server
mcp.description: AI clients such as Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code use this instance through the Model Context Protocol: discover templates, build, check and run workflows, answer approvals, TODOs. Only switchable in the startup configuration.

conversion.name: Run → workflow conversion
conversion.description: Turns a finished run into a reusable workflow.

dialog-import.name: Dialog import
dialog-import.description: Imports a chat dialog and converts it into a workflow.

skills.name: Skills
skills.description: Skill packages and the skill-capability block type.

debug.name: Workflow debugger
debug.description: Lists workflows whose last run failed – with diagnosis and restart.

factory.name: Workflow factory
factory.description: Generates workflows from a description and repairs failing ones on its own.

wishes.name: Wishes
wishes.description: Decomposes free-text goals into workflows and chains.

provenance.name: Definition hash & run provenance
provenance.description: Every run records a SHA-256 hash of the workflow definition, its version and the trigger source.

sealing.name: Sealed workflows
sealing.description: Sealed definitions reject edits and refuse to run once they have been tampered with.

require-sealed-for-unattended.name: Unattended runs only when sealed
require-sealed-for-unattended.description: Unattended runs (schedules, webhooks, triggers, auto-repair, wishes and the chains or sub-workflows they start) only start sealed workflows.

require-signed-seal.name: Seals must be signed
require-signed-seal.description: Sealed workflows need a valid signature (key outside the database). A seal without one, or with a wrong one, refuses its runs.

seal-immutable.name: Unsealing locked
seal-immutable.description: Unsealing is no longer possible through the UI or the API; a seal is released only by someone who can change the startup configuration.

unattended-sandbox.name: Unattended process sandbox
unattended-sandbox.description: AI CLIs and shell blocks outside runs started by a person can neither read nor change or replace the API key file, the seal and integration keys or the database (Linux Landlock). Without Landlock such processes do not start at all.

unattended-in-container.name: Unattended processes in a container
unattended-in-container.description: AI CLIs and shell blocks outside runs started by a person run in a fresh container of the image automation-agent-workflow: only the working directory, the CLI program and its login go in, never the key files, the database or other services of the host user. Without Docker or the image such processes do not start at all.

webhook-signatures.name: Webhook signatures (HMAC)
webhook-signatures.description: Per-webhook signing secret (HMAC-SHA256 in the X-Signature header); a stored secret is always enforced, the switch only gates setting and removing it.

private-network-guard.name: Feeds: no fetches into the local network
private-network-guard.description: iCal feed and RSS/Atom feed fetch public addresses only: targets on localhost, in private networks, link-local (including cloud metadata 169.254.169.254), 0.0.0.0/:: or multicast are refused — the resolved IP addresses are checked, on every redirect too. Turning it off allows local feeds on purpose.

private-network-guard-http-api.name: HTTP API: no fetches into the local network
private-network-guard-http-api.description: The same address check for the HTTP API connection. Off by default, because services in your own network are a common HTTP API target; turned on, it refuses them as well.

private-network-guard-own-services.name: Own services: no fetches into the local network
private-network-guard-own-services.description: The same address check for integrations that talk to a self-hosted service at the address you enter (CalDAV, Gitea/Forgejo, GitLab, ntfy) and for webhook notifications. Off by default, because these services usually run in your own network; turned on, it refuses them as well.
